text:
Priya S: Hi @people-ops — quick question about the year-end shutdown and floating holidays. I joined mid-November and there9s a mandatory shutdown Dec 24-26. Do floating holidays pro-rate for people who start mid-pay-period, and can I use a floating day to extend the shutdown?

Tess (People Ops): Welcome, Priya! Short answer: floating holidays are pro-rated based on your hire date and regional policy. If you joined after the floating holiday allocation date (we run allocations on the first payroll of November), you get a pro-rated allocation. You can request to use a floating holiday to extend the shutdown, but approvals depend on your team coverage.

Priya S: Got it. How does this interact with the company blackout for discretionary PTO? I9d prefer to tack one day onto the shutdown to travel.

Miguel (Eng Manager): From my side: we have a team-level blackout for Dec 24-26, but people generally can request extra days. If it9s not critical coverage-wise, I approve. Please put the PTO request and tag me so I can confirm before payroll lock.

Tess (People Ops): Important nuance: the company blackout blocks auto-approval for discretionary PTO during the core shutdown window so managers can review coverage. It does not ban extensions. Also note: if the floating holiday was not yet allocated (pro-rated case), Payroll will apply the earned portion at the final year payroll. If you request before allocation though, we’ll tentatively approve but final balance depends on payroll posting.

Priya S: Are there regional differences? I9m in EMEA and heard some countries convert unused floating holidays to cash at year-end.

Tess (People Ops): Yes — regional rules differ. EMEA offices have a local conversion policy: up to 8 unused floating hours may be paid out automatically; above that they must be used or they expire (varies by country). US: small balances may convert to float hours or roll over per cap. Check the HR Knowledgebase for country specifics.

Payroll Bot: Note: Payroll cutoff for year-end adjustments is 2025-12-10. Any manual accrual request after this date may not reflect until the next payroll.

Priya S: If payroll posts the wrong pro-rate, what9s the fix path?

Tess (People Ops): Open an HRIS ticket with: employee ID, hire date, pay period, and desired pro-rate. Tag your manager. We coordinate with Payroll for manual adjustments; turnaround is 3-5 business days typically.

Miguel (Eng Manager): Quick admin note — if you9re planning travel, let me know the dates in the PTO request. I9ll try to approve before the payroll cutoff so it9s clear on the balance.

people-ops-bot: Helpful links: https://hr.redwood.example/pto#floating-holidays and https://hr.redwood.example/payroll#year-end-deadlines

Priya S: Perfect, thanks everyone. I9ll put in the PTO request and tag Miguel.

[code block]
Pro-rate example (simple):
- Annual floating days = 1 day (8 hours) allocated Nov payroll
- If hire_date is 2025-11-20 and allocation cutoff = 2025-11-01 -> pro-rate = 8 * (days_employed_in_year / 365) (rounded by payroll rules)
- If allocation happens after request -> manager approval is provisional until payroll posts
[/code block]
